newsitem.title: USA: Chicago to issue $35 mln certificates for building.
newsitem.headline: Chicago to issue $35 mln certificates for building.

text.p: Chicago's City Council voted Wednesday to issue up to $35 million of certificates to buy and renovate a now-vacant building near downtown to relocate city workers from an aging facility in a rapidly developing neighborhood.

Aldermen voted 49-0 to approve the issuance of City of Chicago Building Acquisition Certificates, Series 1997 which will be serviced by operating cost savings realized by the move, said Donal Quinlan, media liaison to the City Council Finance Committee.

As many as 500 city workers will be relocated from the Kraft Building, located in a now hot real estate development district near Lake Michigan, Quinlan said. The city had bought the building in 1981 for $1, but it costs $3.6 million per year to operate, he said.

Under the agreement approved Wednesday, the city will purchase and renovate a former Goldblatt's store in a less congested neighborhood northwest of downtown Chicago, which is expected to cost about $1 million per year to operate, Quinlan said.
The Kraft Building is located on land owned by the Chicago Dock and Canal Trust. Kraft Corp deeded a lease to the property to the city, which expires in 2017.
